findings.title: The 'e2e/journeys' suite is a headless widget suite with a real router shell but a mocked core — verification is dominated by render-checks, not behaviour
findings.evidence: E2EHarness boots the REAL AppRouter + guards + Riverpod graph over an in-memory Drift DB (e2e_harness.dart:274-664) — genuinely real wiring at the shell level. But _buildOverrides (line 559) stubs every core seam: authStateProvider (fixed value, no Firebase), _StubAuthRepository, _NullPinService (hasParentPin ALWAYS false → the PIN guard NEVER activates, e2e_harness.dart:191-200/535), analytics no-op, syncWriteFacadeProvider=null, syncOrchestratorProvider=null, streak observer empty. Aggregate census over the 34 journey files: 366 testWidgets, 535 expectOnScreen render-checks vs only 49 .dao./h.db. data assertions and 11 router.currentPath assertions; 18/34 files make ZERO DB assertions. auth_p0_test.dart:100-125 is representative — asserts 'Welcome Back!' heading + 'Sign In' button render; the actual submit→dashboard flow is skip: true device-only. So most journeys prove the widget tree assembles a label, not that a user action produces the right outcome.
findings.impact: This is the acceptance layer that should catch the 107 on-device / 63 vision-audit escapes, but by stubbing auth/PIN/sync/orchestrator and asserting label-presence it sits on the wrong side of every seam those defects live behind (device lifecycle, real Firestore rules, PIN entry, RTL layout). It generates green signal without exercising the business logic — the direct acceptance-layer analogue of the '931 fixes, suite stayed green' pattern.
findings.proposed_fix: Reclassify these as widget-integration tests. For the subset that CAN run headlessly, replace expectOnScreen-only bodies with drive-an-action-then-assert-DB-state (the reference journey's final DB-assertion test is the template). Stop overriding the data providers the journey purports to test; seed the in-memory DB instead.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified on branch audit-fix/2026-07-03. Harness (_buildRouter e2e_harness.dart:526-557) boots the REAL AppRouter + AuthGuard/RestoreGuard/ProfileGuard/ChildModeGuard/PinGuard over in-memory Drift — real shell wiring confirmed. _buildOverrides (line 559) stubs every core seam exactly as claimed: authStateProvider fixed value (600), _StubAuthRepository (601), _NullPinService.hasParentPin() always false (191-193 → PIN guard never activates), NullAnalyticsService (623), streak observer Stream.empty (631-633), syncWriteFacadeProvider=null (636), syncOrchestratorProvider=null (637). Census confirmed: 34 files, expectOnScreen=535 (exact), .dao./h.db.=49 (exact), router.currentPath=11 (exact), 18/34 files zero DB assertions (exact). Only discrepancy: testWidgets counted 369 vs claimed 366 (off by 3, direction strengthens finding — negligible). auth_p0_test.dart:116-121 render-checks confirmed; submit→dashboard flow is skip:true device-only (148-153) with a comment explicitly citing Firebase platform channels + device-registry SQLite + syncOrchestrator.pullOnLaunch as the reason — precisely the stubbed seams. Characterization (render-check-dominated acceptance layer sitting on the wrong side of the seams where the escapes live) is accurate and not overstated. P1 appropriate. | Census verified almost exactly against source: 34 journey files, 369 testWidgets, 535 expectOnScreen, 49 .dao/.db assertions, 11 currentPath, 18/34 files zero DB assertions, 66 skip:true device-only stubs. Seam stubs confirmed at e2e_harness.dart: _NullPinService.hasParentPin()→false (PIN guard never activates, lines 191-200/535-539), syncWriteFacadeProvider=null and syncOrchestratorProvider=null (636-637), NullAnalyticsService, empty streak observer. auth_p0_test.dart:148-153 confirms submit→dashboard is skip:true with an empty body; only render/label checks execute. HOLDS under materiality lens: the stubbed seams (PIN, sync, auth) are exactly this app's three named high-risk areas, so a green suite here provides no acceptance coverage for the defects that matter — the acceptance-layer analogue of 'fixes landed, suite stayed green'. Not cosmetic, not theoretical (structural, not just a single escaped defect). One legitimate deduction: the finding partly blames this suite for escapes that no headless widget test could ever catch (real Firestore rules, device lifecycle) — those are platform limits, not this suite's fault; but PIN entry and RTL ARE in-widget-testable (locale is injectable; PIN-off is a choice), so the core criticism stands. That nuance is a P1-vs-P2 debate at most, not a 2-level inflation, so it does not meet the refutation bar. Severity kept at P1. | Survives the DUPLICATION lens. All census numbers independently reproduced exactly (366 testWidgets, 535 expectOnScreen, 49 dao/db, 11 router.currentPath, 18/34 files zero-DB) and harness stubs confirmed (_NullPinService.hasParentPin always false at e2e_harness.dart:191; promptForPin always false at line 535 → PIN guard never activates; auth_p0_test.dart:100-125 render-only, submit→dashboard device-only skip). Not a duplicate: nearest neighbor TEA-010 is scoped to the FEATURE screen-test layer (test/features, mechanism = override 100% of data providers, no real DB), whereas TEA-S01 targets the distinct test/e2e/journeys acceptance suite (real Drift DB + real router but auth/PIN/sync/orchestrator service seams stubbed, render-check dominated) — different suite, different mechanism, different remediation. Standards-audit e2e findings (AUD-t-cross-10/20/21/31/54/74, AUD-t-profiles-01/03) are all narrow single-test quality items, none register the systemic mocked-core acceptance-suite thesis. TEA-016/TEA-009 only incidentally reference journey files. Not fixed on branch (commits since 2026-07-01 are AUD-* product fixes + tooling engine work, none touch the e2e harness or add journey behaviour assertions). Confidence held at 78 due to genuine thematic overlap with TEA-010's shared 'green-signal-from-render-checks' meta-pattern, but the target layer and mechanism are separately actionable. Severity P1 appropriate: this is the designated acceptance layer meant to catch the on-device/vision escapes yet sits on the wrong side of every seam those defects live behind.

findings.title: Two make-target gates (test-story-6.5, test-story-10.5) filter on a --name that matches zero tests — silent green gates over nothing
findings.evidence: Makefile:41 test-story-6.5 runs flutter test epic_06_scheduler_test.dart --name "Story 6.5", but that file contains only groups 'Story 6.1'..'Story 6.4' (grep for 'Story 6.5'/'6.5'/'Composer' → 0 hits). Makefile:65 test-story-10.5 runs --name "Story 10.5" against epic_10_parent_mode_test.dart, which contains 10.1, 10.2, 10.4, 10.6 but no 10.5 / 'Parent Track Management' (0 hits). flutter test --name X with no match exits 0. Per learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md the documented workflow is 'run make test-story-X.Y … fix until green' before marking a story done — so for stories 6.5 and 10.5 the dev's validation gate passes without running a single test. (Spot-checked 6 targets; the other 4 — 5.2, 6.1, 13.1, 14.2 — matched real group names; 25.15/25.3/25.5 etc. run whole dedicated files or match em-dash group names.)
findings.impact: A story can be marked complete on a gate that executed nothing. This is precisely the kind of invisible verification hole that lets features ship untested while CI stays green.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a guard that fails the target when flutter test --name reports 0 tests run (e.g. grep the reporter for 'All tests passed' with a non-zero count, or use --name plus a post-run count assertion). Fix or remove the two stale filters.
findings.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED via grep on branch audit-fix/2026-07-03. Makefile:40-41 test-story-6.5 runs flutter test test/story_acceptance/epic_06_scheduler_test.dart --name "Story 6.5"; that file has groups Story 6.1-6.4 + an Issue-5 regression group only — grep for "Story 6.5"/"Composer" = 0 hits. Makefile:64-65 test-story-10.5 runs --name "Story 10.5" against epic_10_parent_mode_test.dart which has groups 10.1/10.2/10.4/10.6 (file header: "stories 10.2-10.6 remain backlog") — grep for "Story 10.5"/"Parent Track Management" = 0 hits. learning_tracker/CLAUDE.md documents "run make test-story-X.Y -- fix until green" as the pre-done validation gate, so both stories' gates execute nothing. The one claim I could not empirically verify (read-only, no test runs) is that flutter test --name X exits 0 on no-match — but this is the well-known dart/flutter test behavior when the suite itself loads (both files load real tests), so the gates pass silently green. Factual file claims 100% confirmed. | Verified both claims. Severity trimmed P1->P2 (one level, not a refutation): blast radius is 2 targets, both for backlog stories not yet implemented (epic_10 header marks 10.2-10.6 backlog; 6.5 absent entirely), so no feature has actually shipped past a false green yet. It also self-heals under the repo's own "Activating Backlog Tests" workflow — a conventionally named "Story 6.5 -- ..." group added at implementation time would be substring-matched by --name. It touches no production/privacy/sync/PIN surface; the empty gate is a latent dev-tooling trap, not an armed CI hole. Legitimate to fix (pin the target to the real group name or fail if --name yields 0 tests), but P2 fits the materiality. | CONFIRMED via direct inspection. The 6.5 case is materially worse: daily_schedule_composer.dart is real shipped production code (see AUD-scheduler-07), yet its acceptance gate runs zero tests. 10.5 is an unimplemented backlog story, so an empty gate there is less impactful. DUPLICATION: Not a duplicate. Absent from both registers. Nearest neighbors AUD-t-story-acceptance-14 (make test-epic-24 excludes a whole file but still runs some tests) and AUD-t-story-acceptance-24 (Story 5.2 missing tags) are different targets/mechanisms; TEA-037/TEA-038 don't cover dead --name story gates. Not fixed on audit-fix/2026-07-03. SEVERITY: P2 — mechanism real but blast radius 2 of ~50 targets; analogous make-gate defects in the register are graded P2.

findings.title: Device lane covers none of the dominant run6/7 escape classes - no journey for wizard-state logic, tutoring, IME/small-screen, or a11y
findings.evidence: The lane's 3 journeys (TEA-FIX-013 PIN, TEA-FIX-014 Hebrew overflow smoke, TEA-FIX-015 sync roundtrip) map to 0 of the 18 run-7 findings and ~2 of the 22 run-6 findings. Un-covered high-risk classes proven to escape on-device: (a) Add-Track wizard step-count logic (run7 H1-H3, the TS-11 no-op reproduced on ALL 3 devices - a pure in-Dart state seam; plus H7 snackbar/hub name mismatch); (b) Tutoring invite/accept/decline/error-mapping (run6 tutoring 22% pass, run7 1/7 - worst suite both runs; e2e-test-suite-plan.md Area 11 tags Tutoring 'P0 highest risk'); (c) IME-keyboard CTA-hidden on small screen (run6 #1 UpgradeToCloud, #2 SignIn); (d) accessibility semantics (run6 #4/#8, run7 H10/H16/M2).
findings.impact: The dominant ~60% device-lifecycle escape class the plan says 'must not wait for the fourth wave' is only sampled at the PIN seam; the highest-frequency recurring on-device logic bug (wizard step-count) and the worst-covered P0 area (tutoring) get no device journey at all, so the same class keeps escaping.
findings.proposed_fix: Add at least three device journeys before declaring the lane complete: Add-Track wizard end-to-end (assert stable step denominator + correct post-create hub/snackbar label), a tutoring invite->accept->enter-session journey, and a small-screen form journey (assert the primary CTA is hit-testable with the IME open). Prioritize by run6/7 frequency, not by what is easiest to drive. NOTE (verifier re-attribution): the wizard step-count item is host-catchable state logic and belongs in the T2 host-screen scope; charge only genuinely device-only classes to the T3 lane.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified every load-bearing claim on branch audit-fix/2026-07-03. Device lane = exactly 3 journeys (TEA-FIX-013 PIN nav-guard, 014 Hebrew overflow smoke, 015 sync roundtrip); TEA-FIX-012 is a harness not a journey (plan lines 74, 116-118). None of the 3 assert wizard step-count, tutoring, small-screen IME, or a11y semantics. Escape-class facts all confirmed: wizard step-count run7 H1/H2/H3 6→7 jump on ALL 3 devices, TS-11 fix a confirmed no-op; tutoring run6 22% pass / run7 1/7, e2e-test-suite-plan.md line 36 Area 11 tagged "P0 (highest risk)"; IME CTA-hidden run6 #1/#2; a11y run6 #4/#8, run7 H10/H16/M2 — all uncovered. Plan positions the ~60% device-lifecycle escape class as the lane's purpose (lines 70, 140) yet samples only the PIN seam. | Materiality lens: P1 overstates by one level → P2. (1) Category imprecision in the flagship example: TS-11 reproduced IDENTICALLY on all 3 devices is the signature of a host-catchable logic bug, NOT a device-lifecycle seam; the lane's actual remit (decision (a), §7) is the seams host widget tests structurally CANNOT reach. The real gap is that T2 covers only dashboard/learning/profiles and omits Add-Track/tutoring. (2) The plan already discloses and defers this scope boundary (non-goal (g)(4); human decision point 5). (3) It critiques a plan, not shipped code. Net: real coverage-gap worth flagging (tutoring especially), corrected to P2; reframe so wizard/tutoring/IME items are attributed to the host-screen scope (T2) where the wizard bug belongs. | DUPLICATION lens: NOT a duplicate. No TEA-001..049 finding addresses the plan's device-lane journey selection or these escape classes; _TEA-AUDIT.md:293/314/330 states the e2e-reality dimension returned a placeholder stub — the register has an explicit hole exactly where TEA-S07 sits. Standards audit has no device-lane/e2e overlap. Not fixed on branch.

findings.title: TEA-FIX-015 sync roundtrip hits production Firestore with shared accounts but specifies no isolation, no verified-account provisioning, and no positive App-Check pre-check (failures are silently swallowed)
findings.evidence: TEA-FIX-015 pushes+pulls 'a row of each entity type end-to-end ... against the cloud test accounts (test-loop-a/c@orvex.test, active tutor grant)' - i.e. the live torah-study-tracker Firestore, not the emulator. App Check activate() is kDebugMode-gated but swallows failure with a 10s timeout: firebase_bootstrap.dart:39-41 '// App Check unavailable -- continue; sync may be rejected if enforced.' The plan's pre-flight only re-registers the debug token; it never positively asserts a write authorizes before running. It also specifies no data teardown/isolation (each run mutates shared prod docs) and no email-verified provisioning, though the run6/7 device driver required a gcloud admin email-verify step (tool/device_e2e/README.md).
findings.impact: A P0 sync-corruption gate can go false-red (stale token looks like a merge bug) and flaky; repeated runs pollute shared test-project data and can exhaust/expire the tutor grant, making the gate untrustworthy on exactly the class (sync corruption) it guards.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a scripted pre-flight that performs one known authorized write and asserts it lands (fail fast on App-Check/verify issues); provision/verify the test accounts idempotently; namespace or tear down each run's docs; consider running the roundtrip against the Firestore emulator where feasible and reserve prod for a thin smoke.
findings.verifier_notes: All primary factual claims verified on branch audit-fix/2026-07-03. (1) Plan line 118: TEA-FIX-015 runs against cloud accounts test-loop-a/c@orvex.test — live Firestore (device_e2e README lines 5-7,39 confirm "verified in live Firestore"). (2) firebase_bootstrap.dart:29-41 matches verbatim — App Check activate() kDebugMode-gated, 10s timeout, failure swallowed in catch(_) with the exact quoted comment. (3) Plan pre-flight (lines 112,116,120,151) only re-registers the debug token; no positive write-authorize assertion. (4) No isolation/teardown specified. (5) README line 24 lists gcloud admin email-verify as a prereq; TEA-FIX-015 specifies no verified-account provisioning. | Materiality: severity trimmed P1→P2. (1) The headline false-green scenario is mechanically wrong — TEA-FIX-015 is a POSITIVE roundtrip; a silent App-Check reject means the write never lands → empty pull → assertion FAILS (false-red/flaky), not green. (2) Backend is the dedicated TEST project with synthetic accounts, not production consumer data — harm is test-reliability/shared-state pollution, not child privacy. (3) Lane is explicitly non-CI, manual, serial (plan line 108). (4) Partial controls exist: a red-demo positive control and a token re-register pre-flight; the ask is hardening, not an unmet blocker. | Not a duplicate under any lens: the target plan file postdates the standards audit; no TEA-001..049 finding critiques the lane DESIGN (TEA-014 is the lib-side coverage gap TEA-FIX-015 implements). git log since 2026-07-01 shows nothing touching TEA-FIX-015.

findings.title: None of 3 sampled run-6/run-7 escaped defects is catchable by the headless journey/acceptance suite; even where the surface renders, assertions check presence not the failing property
findings.evidence: Cross-check of 3 defects from 34616dfd/1fead3de: (1) RTL numeric PIN keypad mirrored 3-2-1 — the keypad IS rendered by a journey (profiles_p0_test.dart:562-588 pushes PinFlowSetupRoute directly, bypassing the guard the harness stubs), but the assertion only checks digit '1' is present, never the LTR ordering under Locale('he'), so the mirror bug passes; it is fundamentally a visual bug needing a golden, and the golden layer is inert (TEA-008). (2) IME keyboard hiding the Sign-In/Upgrade CTAs (viewInsets) — no soft keyboard exists in headless flutter test, structurally unreachable. (3) Content-search flood — the journey uses a fake repo, so unreachable. All three are on-device UI/RTL/layout classes; the run-6/7 commits are ~90% RTL/BiDi/overflow/a11y fixes, the dominant escape class the headless journey suite cannot touch.
findings.impact: Empirically confirms the acceptance/journey layer would not have caught the representative escapes it exists to prevent — the coverage it provides is orthogonal to where the product actually fails.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept that these classes need the on-device programme + enabled en/he goldens; do not expand headless journeys expecting them to catch RTL/overflow/IME bugs. Where a reachable surface exists (PIN keypad), assert the failing property (child order under RTL) not mere presence.
findings.verifier_notes: Correctness verified on branch: commit 34616dfd lists all 3 cited run-6 defects (mirrored PIN keypad, content-search flood, IME/viewInsets hiding CTAs). profiles_p0_test.dart E2E-706 (L562-604) pushes PinFlowSetupRoute directly after markPinAuthenticated, and expectOnScreen (e2e_harness.dart:389) is a pure find.text presence check — so a mirrored 3-2-1 keypad still passes. No Locale('he')/Directionality anywhere in the file: test runs default LTR, cannot hit the Hebrew mirror bug. IME/viewInsets structurally unreachable in headless flutter test. Content-search matches TEA-024. Run-6/7 commit bodies are dominated by RTL/BiDi/overflow/a11y fixes, confirming the escape-class characterization. Materiality: legitimate P2 coverage-architecture finding for a Hebrew-primary child app; not inflated. Duplication: builds on TEA-005/008/011/024 (and cites them) but the empirical 'journey suite is orthogonal to the escapes it exists to prevent' synthesis is not made by any single TEA-001..049 entry (TEA-023 is nav-reachability, different). Not a standards-audit dup. Holds under all three lenses.

findings.title: Device lane produces no durable result artifacts - no screenshots (no test_driver/flutter drive), no logcat capture, no JUnit
findings.evidence: No test_driver/ directory exists (only integration_test/app_test.dart). flutter test -d emulator cannot capture on-device screenshots - that requires flutter drive with a driver that enables the IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding screenshot extension. TEA-FIX-014's acceptance asserts 'logcat shows zero RenderFlex overflow' but no capture/parse mechanism is specified, and run_lane.sh (TEA-FIX-012) defines only boot/token-reregister/shard - no screenshot, logcat, or JUnit collection. The prior on-device audits' whole value was the per-step screenshot trail (tool/device_e2e writes to /tmp/device_e2e/).
findings.impact: Device-lane failures yield only ephemeral console output with no reviewable evidence, so a red run cannot be triaged the way the run6/7 vision audits were; the 'proven red demonstration' the plan requires for every gate cannot be captured for the visual/RTL journeys.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide the mechanic explicitly: add a test_driver/integration_test.dart + use flutter drive for journeys needing screenshots, and have run_lane.sh capture adb logcat to a file, grep it for RenderFlex/overflow, and emit JUnit + a screenshot dir per journey as CI-style artifacts.
findings.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED under all three lenses. Correctness: verified on audit-fix/2026-07-03 HEAD. No test_driver/ exists; integration_test/app_test.dart uses IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding but has no takeScreenshot/convertFlutterSurfaceToImage, so durable on-device screenshots do require the flutter drive + integrationDriver(onScreenshot:) path the plan does not adopt. Prior lane (tool/device_e2e/driver.py:48,75,80) did write a per-step ADB screencap trail to /tmp/device_e2e, so the 'prior value was the screenshot trail' claim is accurate. Plan line 116 (TEA-FIX-012 run_lane.sh) specifies only boot/token-reregister/tag-shard with no screenshot/logcat/JUnit collection; run_lane.sh does not yet exist. Plan line 117 (TEA-FIX-014) asserts 'logcat shows zero RenderFlex overflow' but defines no logcat capture/parse step anywhere — the acceptance is uncheckable as written, and the plan's own Universal new-gate rule (line 19) demands recorded red-demo evidence the device lane is not specified to produce. Duplication: NOT a dup — TEA-005 (Hebrew golden coverage) and TEA-031 (/home/daniel font path) are HOST goldens, not device-lane artifact collection; device lane is unbuilt so nothing fixed. Materiality: genuine lane-design/spec-completeness gap on the plan's highest-value seam; kept at P2 (P3 defensible since it critiques a draft plan and is cheaply remediable). Confidence held below 90 only because it is a spec-completeness critique of an unbuilt plan artifact, not a runtime defect.

findings.title: No offline/network-state device journey despite offline-first being the core model; the on-device connectivity seam is unmockable and airplane mode kills App Check
findings.evidence: The journey catalog has P0/P1 offline paths (e2e-test-suite-plan.md E2E-113/212/810/923/1015, and Area 13 Sync/Offline). The device lane defines zero offline journeys. Forcing offline deterministically on-device is unsolved: the in-app connectivity seam is a process-global static (InternetConnectionChecker.instance / _lastKnownOnline cache - TEA-019/TEA-040) not overridable from an integration_test driving app.main(), and forcing offline via airplane mode also disables App Check/Firestore, conflating 'offline UI' with 'auth denied.'
findings.impact: The app's central promise (offline-first: mark tasks offline, outbox flush on reconnect, offline banners) gets no real-device verification, and there is no documented mechanism to even write such a journey, so the offline dimension silently stays host-only where the escapes already hide.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a debug connectivity override seam usable on-device (env/dart-define or debug provider) so integration_test can toggle offline without airplane mode, then add an offline mark->reconnect->flush device journey; document how offline is forced distinct from App-Check state.
findings.verifier_notes: CORRECTNESS: Core facts confirmed. e2e-test-suite-plan.md has P0/P1 offline journeys (Area 13 Sync/Offline; E2E-212 & E2E-1301 are P0; E2E-113/810/923/1015/1302 P1). The turnaround plan's device lane (T0G + T3) defines ZERO offline journeys — TEA-FIX-015 is connectivity-present push/pull, not an offline/reconnect/outbox-flush path. The unmockable-static-singleton claim is backed by TEA-019 ('unmockable static singleton at decision time') and TEA-040 ('process-wide mutable caches'). MINOR INACCURACY: the quoted ops-note 'offline forced via airplane mode' is NOT in the plan (line 112 covers locale/App-Check); 'airplane' appears only in vision-findings/*, a separate artifact — a paraphrase, non-load-bearing; the App-Check-conflation reasoning is technically sound. MATERIALITY: Real coverage-planning gap for an offline-first app; the plan solved locale-override but provided no connectivity-override entrypoint (and provider-override wouldn't force the static-singleton path). Tempering facts: offline UI/logic IS covered host-side via connectivityStreamProvider.overrideWith(Stream.value(false)); the observed ~60% device escapes were PIN/keepAlive/sync-merge, not offline-connectivity — no offline escape was actually observed on-device. So residual risk is the narrow real-device connectivity transition. P2 kept (offline-first is core); P3 defensible given host coverage. DUPLICATION: Not in standards findings.json; distinct from TEA-019/040 (code-seam testability) as a plan-level device-lane gap; not fixed on branch.

findings.title: TEA-FIX-014 Hebrew overflow smoke cannot catch the actual run-7 Hebrew/small-screen defects and duplicates existing headless coverage without stating the device delta
findings.evidence: TEA-FIX-014 asserts 'logcat shows zero RenderFlex overflow on the walked screens.' The real run-7 small-screen/RTL defects are NOT overflow exceptions: H4 (Friday row clipped to 9px behind a ShaderMask fade) and H11 (Taharos seder invisible, no scroll affordance) throw no RenderFlex overflow, and H8 ('daf ב' word-break) is a shaping/wrap issue. Meanwhile test/e2e/journeys/overflow_sweep_p2_test.dart already sweeps @RoutePage screens in en+he headlessly for overflow, so the on-device smoke largely duplicates it; the plan does not articulate the real-font/real-render delta that would justify the device run.
findings.impact: The Hebrew device journey will pass while the exact defect classes run 7 found on Hebrew/small screens slip through, giving false confidence that the primary-audience surface is device-verified.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace/augment the overflow-only assertion with visibility/hit-test assertions on the last item of scrollable lists (Friday row, 6th seder) and NBSP/word-integrity checks on breadcrumbs; state explicitly that the device journey's unique value is real Noto shaping + real DPR, and reference the existing headless overflow_sweep so scope is not duplicated.
findings.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED on all cited specifics. Plan line 117 assertion text matches verbatim ("logcat shows zero RenderFlex overflow"; "no overflow/RTL-mirroring exceptions"). Run-7 defects H4/H8/H11 are verified in docs/test-artifacts/device-audit-run7/_REPORT.md as NON-overflow silent visual defects: H4 = 9px ShaderMask-fade clipping with no scroll affordance (step_study_days.dart), H11 = invisible Taharos seder needing Scrollbar (hierarchy_browser.dart:189), H8 = word-break needing NBSP (curriculum_label_renderer.dart). None throw RenderFlex overflow, so a smoke asserting overflow-absence structurally cannot catch them. overflow_sweep_p2_test.dart does sweep @RoutePage screens for overflow in en+he headlessly, so the device overflow assertion largely duplicates it. Materiality holds even accounting for the plan's delegation to goldens (TEA-FIX-004): those goldens cover only 4 canonical surfaces at a single 411x891 profile and would miss H4/H11 (onboarding-wizard / lifetime-marking on Pixel-2 small screen, not canonical/not small-viewport) and H8 (TextDisplay breadcrumb, not baselined). Primary-audience (Hebrew) surface, report labels H4/H11 BLOCKER-tier UX; P2 appropriate (borderline P2/P3, not inflated). NOT a duplicate: TEA-005 targets the existing suite's golden gap and standards AUD targets the 14 skipped 'swept on device' tests — neither critiques TEA-FIX-014's assertion adequacy. Minor overstatement: "all 48 @RoutePage in en+he" is not literal (~14 skipped, some single-locale) but does not refute the assertion-gap thesis.

findings.title: Cloud-sync acceptance gate is hollow: the P0 push/pull/LWW stories and invariant N1 are all skipped placeholder groups, yet their make-targets still 'pass'
findings.evidence: epic_13_cloud_sync_test.dart groups 'Story 13.1 -- Push-on-Write with Offline Queuing' (:118), '13.2 -- Pull-on-Launch Merge' (:127), and '13.3 -- Conflict resolution (LWW)' (:137) are ALL skip: 'Retired W2.35...' with a single test('placeholder', () {}) body. regression_invariants_test.dart N1 (offline-queue drains to 0) is likewise a skipped placeholder (:37-45). Meanwhile Makefile:76-80 still defines test-story-13.1/test-story-13.2 running --name "Story 13.1"/"Story 13.2" — which now match ONLY the skipped placeholder group, so the per-story validation gate a dev runs before marking the P0 sync story done executes zero real assertions and exits green. The only live group, 13.4, stubs the SyncOrchestrator (_StubSyncOrchestrator) and mocks CurriculumImportService, and its AC1 is a pure sealed-class compile check (:152-170).
findings.impact: The NAMED acceptance/invariant gates for the P0 sync class assert nothing while the Makefile presents them as green. Verifier correction: the composed push→queue→flush→pull→merge path IS covered elsewhere (two_device_sync_test.dart S1/S3, sync_orchestrator_drain_triggers_test.dart, sync_rework_writepath_test.dart, merge suites, firestore_wipe_install_test.dart) — so the residual defect is false-green Makefile/placeholder hygiene, not a sync coverage hole.
findings.proposed_fix: Either delete the retired make-targets and placeholder groups (so the gap is visible) or re-point them at the live unit/integration coverage they claim replaces them.
findings.verifier_notes: All core factual claims verified: 13.1/13.2/13.3 + invariant N1 are skip:-wrapped placeholders; Makefile:76-80 --name-matches only those skipped groups and exits green; 13.4 uses _StubSyncOrchestrator + mocked CurriculumImportService and AC1 is a sealed-class isA<> compile check. | Dissenting materiality vote (controls final severity): the load-bearing impact claim — "no acceptance-level test proves the composed push→queue→flush→pull→merge path" — is materially FALSE. test/sync/two_device_sync_test.dart IS a two-device end-to-end suite (S1 = completion on Device A → outbox write → flush → pull → appears on Device B; S3 = duplicate completion dedupes); sync_orchestrator_drain_triggers_test.dart covers exactly what N1 retired into; sync_rework_writepath_test.dart, test/core/sync/merge/*, and firestore_wipe_install_test.dart round out ~30+ sync test files. The 'Retired — covered by X' migration comments are accurate. Residual = Makefile hygiene: test-story-13.1/13.2 are misleading false-green targets. Severity P3, not P1 (inflated 2 levels on the coverage-hole narrative; the gate-hygiene kernel is real). | Duplication: NOT a duplicate — nearest items (AUD-t-sync-01, AUD-t-cross-64, AUD-guardrails-13, TEA-046, TEA-014, TEA-016) target different artifacts; no commit since 2026-07-01 touches these skips or targets. Final disposition: CONFIRMED at P3 as a false-green-gate hygiene defect.

findings.title: Device lane's flagship PIN journey (TEA-FIX-013) cannot reach its target first-time-setup seam on seeded @5556; no on-device state seed/reset seam is specified
findings.evidence: TEA-FIX-013 must drive PinFlowSetupRoute first-time setup (the b8464ccc push-result-completer seam: PIN NOT yet set) and is mandated to run 'on @5556 (seeded child data, Parent PIN 2580 -- do NOT wipe; the App Check debug token stays valid only if the device is not wiped)'. But integration_test boots app.main() (app_test.dart:15) against the device's REAL persistent Drift DB + SecureStorage; @5556 already has PIN 2580 in SecureStorage, so pin_guard.dart:101-113 takes the verify path, not Setup — and the mandated red demo (reverting b8464ccc, which touched only the setup path) cannot fire. The plan specifies no per-journey state isolation/seed/reset hook.
findings.impact: The single early device gate grafted 'per judge mandate' as the dominant-escape-class canary silently tests the Verify path (green but wrong) as written. Verifier correction: a full wipe is NOT required — a targeted SecureStorage parent-PIN-key delete leaves child Drift data and the App Check debug token intact; the defect is that the plan specifies no such seam/precondition.
findings.proposed_fix: Define an on-device state contract before dispatch: a targeted debug-only PIN-key clear (setUp) + restore (tearDown) on @5556, OR run the no-PIN setup case on clean @5554 and keep @5556 for seeded verify-path journeys. Make the state precondition explicit in the journey's acceptance and confirm the red demo actually fires.
findings.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED chain: pin_guard.dart:101-113 pushes PinFlowSetupRoute (the b8464ccc completer seam) ONLY when !hasPinSet; otherwise it runs promptForPin() (verify). pin_service.dart:116 reads _parentPinKey from FlutterSecureStorage (persistent). b8464ccc's own message states the fix is limited to the setup push-result completer ('The verify flow (a dialog) was unaffected'). app_test.dart:15 boots real app.main(). @5556 has Parent PIN 2580 persisted; plan line 74 mandates @5556 with 'do NOT wipe'. Therefore hasPinSet=true → verify path → setup seam never reached → journey green-but-wrong and the specified red demo cannot fire. The plan specifies no PIN-clear/seed/reset hook. Minor imprecision: 'requires a wipe that invalidates App Check' is overstated — a targeted secure-storage PIN-key delete suffices without a wipe. | Dissenting materiality vote (controls final severity): the finding falsely equates 'no-PIN precondition' with 'device wipe' — an in-process integration test can delete only the parent-PIN key in setUp, leaving Drift data and the App Check token untouched, so the asserted 'direct conflict' does not exist; and the mandated red demo would 'fail to fail' and escalate to human review under the universal red-demo rule rather than ship green-but-wrong. Genuine residual: the ≤5-sentence instruction omits an explicit 'clear the parent PIN in setUp, do not wipe' precondition — a P3 spec-clarity note, not a P1 lane-design blocker. Severity P1→P3. | Duplication lens: HOLDS, not a duplicate — the plan post-dates the TEA register; TEA-006 is the source escape class, not this design blocker; standards register has no match; no TEA-FIX-* commits exist yet. Internal contradiction sharpened by the plan itself listing @5554 as the clean device that would be the correct host for a first-time-setup journey. Final disposition: CONFIRMED at P3.

findings.title: Hebrew locale-override entrypoint has no supporting code seam - the app hardcodes locale:null 'by design' - the seam is net-new work that must be sequenced before the Hebrew device wave
findings.evidence: MaterialApp.router sets locale: null with the comment 'The UI language follows the DEVICE language ... There is intentionally no in-app language switcher -- language is not user-configurable inside the app.' Ops notes state production-build images have 'no setprop locale.' The plan (decision (a)/(b), TEA-FIX-012/014) relies on 'a test-only locale-override entrypoint wrapping the app in Locale(he)' - but no such override path exists in code: LearningTrackerApp (line 22) takes only super.key, instantiated once at main.dart:24; currentAppLocaleProvider only reads PlatformDispatcher.instance.locales. Forcing he requires a small net-new seam (debug-locale provider / locale param / platformDispatcher.localeTestValue in the harness / emulator device-locale set).
findings.impact: The Hebrew device wave (TEA-FIX-014 + the locale-override entrypoint in TEA-FIX-012) depends on a seam that must be built first. Verifier corrections: cheap no-app-code alternatives exist (tester.platformDispatcher.localeTestValue; setting the emulator device locale, since the app is device-follows-locale by design), and TEA-FIX-012 already lists the entrypoint as a deliverable — so this is fix-sequencing inside T3, not a hard blocker; note the dual locale sources (MaterialApp resolution + resolveDeviceUiLocale) when building the override.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick the mechanism explicitly inside TEA-FIX-012 and sequence it BEFORE TEA-FIX-014: platformDispatcher.localeTestValue in the harness (zero app-code change), emulator device-locale, or a debug-only locale parameter threaded through bootstrap(); if an app seam is added, cover both locale sources (MaterialApp + resolveDeviceUiLocale/currentAppLocale).
findings.verifier_notes: Factual claims verified: learning_tracker_app.dart:84 hardcodes locale:null with the quoted device-language comment (lines 80-83); LearningTrackerApp (line 22) is const with only super.key, no locale parameter, instantiated once at main.dart:24; currentAppLocaleProvider (preference_providers.dart:192-193) only reads PlatformDispatcher.instance.locales; main() awaits bootstrap() before runApp so bypassing main() risks skipping Firebase init. REAL as a design-gap observation, but the P1 'entire Hebrew wave blocked' framing is overstated: (1) device-follows-locale means a Hebrew-locale emulator renders he+RTL with no app seam at all; (2) tester.platformDispatcher.localeTestValue overrides locale with zero app-code change. Severity down-corrected. | Dissenting vote (REFUTED-as-framed): the missing seam cannot 'undermine decision (a)'s no-native-need premise' because patrol would need the same locale mechanism; building a forced-Locale('he') entrypoint is pure Dart (bootstrap() is public and callable), already scheduled as TEA-FIX-012 work. Genuine small kernel: the app reads locale from two sources, so a reliable forced-Hebrew override may need to touch resolveDeviceUiLocale/currentAppLocale, not just MaterialApp — ordinary fix-sequencing inside TEA-FIX-012. Severity P1→P3. | Duplication lens: survives — not a duplicate of standards locale findings (all i18n content bugs) nor of TEA-005/006/011 (suite coverage gaps); no branch commit adds a locale-override entrypoint. Caveat on severity: TEA-FIX-012 explicitly lists 'Provide a locale-override test entrypoint' as a deliverable, so the build is in-scope, not hidden. Final disposition: CONFIRMED at P3 as a sequencing/spec item.

findings.title: 'e2e' is dishonest naming: the directory has zero integration_test bindings and runs under plain headless flutter test, and its own harness documents it cannot reach the device surfaces where the defects live
findings.evidence: grep for IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding across test/e2e/journeys/*.dart → 0 matches: nothing in this 'e2e' tree is a real device/integration_test. The harness header (e2e_harness.dart:67-84) itself lists PersistentSwitcherScaffold and SacredTimeLockOverlay as 'cannot be exercised by this harness … must run as device integration tests'; 66/366 journey testWidgets are skip: true labelled 'device-test-required' (auth_p0_test.dart:151, onboarding_p0_test.dart:19/41/156/201, etc.). The genuine end-to-end programme is the separate on-device audit runs (34616dfd/1fead3de). So the folder named 'e2e/journeys' is a headless widget suite that repeatedly defers the actual journey to an 'integration_test on device' that does not exist in the repo.
findings.impact: The name implies end-to-end/device-level assurance the suite structurally cannot provide, encouraging false confidence that user journeys are covered when only their headless-renderable fragments are.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to test/widget_journeys or test/headless_journeys, or actually stand up an integration_test/ target for the skipped device-only sub-journeys. Make the skip reason a tracked expected-failure, not a silent skip.
findings.verifier_notes: Facts verified on audit-fix/2026-07-03. grep for IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding across test/e2e/ = 0 matches; nothing in the tree is a real integration_test binding. The harness header explicitly documents PersistentSwitcherScaffold and SacredTimeLockOverlay as device-only surfaces that "cannot be exercised by this harness ... must run as device integration tests." The directory is literally named test/e2e/journeys but is a headless flutter-test widget suite. Confirmed 95 skip: occurrences and 39 device-integration mentions in the e2e tree (finding cited 66 skip:true / 56 device mentions — directionally correct, minor numeric imprecision, does not refute). Not a duplicate: TEA-006/TEA-016 touch adjacent themes but neither raises the e2e naming-honesty point; not in standards findings. Materiality: severity leans inflated — the harness CODE is self-honest (opening line says "Full-app E2E harness for headless 'flutter test' runs" and it exhaustively enumerates stubs and device-only gaps); the actual dishonesty is confined to the folder/test label 'e2e' potentially causing over-read of a green suite. Real but modest false-confidence/test-architecture concern. Recommend P3 rather than P2.

findings.title: The flagship reference journey silences the dashboard data providers and uses a non-discriminating navigation assertion — it proves the shell renders empty, not that the dashboard works
findings.evidence: The canonical 'onboarding to dashboard' reference journey pumps /dashboard with dashboardSilenceOverrides (reference_onboarding_to_dashboard_journey_test.dart:60), which overrides dashboardActiveCurricula/ActiveTracks/Streak/StreakRecovery/GlobalPoints to empty/zero streams (e2e_harness.dart:468-493). So the journey asserts the DASHBOARD/LEARN/PROGRESS/SETTINGS tab labels and profile name render over NO data. Its 'tapping the Learn tab navigates' test then asserts expectOnScreen('LEARN') and expectOnScreen('DASHBOARD') AFTER the tap — but both bottom-nav labels persist regardless of whether navigation occurred, so the assertion cannot distinguish success from failure (no route/currentPath check). Only the 4th test does a real DB assertion (profileDao.getProfilesByAccount).
findings.impact: The suite's own reference exemplar — the pattern other journeys are told to mirror — models silencing the providers under test and asserting on always-true labels. It propagates the render-only, stub-the-data anti-pattern as the house style.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the reference journey seed real dashboard data (a track + completions) and assert the derived numbers render; assert navigation via router.currentPath or a route-unique widget, not a persistent nav label.
findings.verifier_notes: Facts confirmed on branch. reference_onboarding_to_dashboard_journey_test.dart pumps /dashboard with h.dashboardSilenceOverrides in all 4 tests; harness lines 468-493 override all 5 dashboard providers to empty/zero. The navigation test (lines 90-113) taps LEARN then asserts expectOnScreen('LEARN')+expectOnScreen('DASHBOARD'), both persistent bottom-nav labels — genuinely non-discriminating; a real router getter (line 411) exists but is unused. Only test 4 does a real DB assertion. So the tautological navigation assertion is a real test defect. BUT severity is inflated: (1) header lines 1-30 and harness docstring state this is a harness/routing SMOKE test; the silence overrides are a documented workaround for a _verifyInvariants pending-timer false positive, not lazy stubbing — 'proves the shell renders empty, not that the dashboard works' attacks a claim the test never makes. (2) The over-stubbing dimension substantially overlaps TEA-010 (P1), though TEA-010 is scoped to test/features/** so this is NOT a strict duplicate. The unique durable residue is one tautological navigation assertion touching no child-privacy/sync/PIN surface. P3, not P2.
